candidates.violated_requirement: Gray-to-binary conversion should use XOR for each bit. Replacing XOR with OR in the second bit conversion will produce incorrect binary values, leading to wrong Gray code output after the full conversion cycle.
candidates.spec_basis: The implementation should follow this process: 1. Input a Gray code value, 2. Convert the Gray code to binary representation using XOR operations

candidates.violated_requirement: Final bit of Gray-to-binary conversion should use XOR. Using AND instead will cause incorrect binary values, affecting the subsequent increment and Gray code conversion.
candidates.spec_basis: The implementation should follow this process: 1. Input a Gray code value, 2. Convert the Gray code to binary representation using XOR operations

candidates.violated_requirement: Binary-to-Gray conversion requires XOR between adjacent bits. Using AND instead will produce incorrect Gray code values that don't follow the single-bit change property.
candidates.spec_basis: Gray code is a binary numeral system where two successive values differ in only one bit position

candidates.violated_requirement: MSB of Gray-to-binary conversion should pass through unchanged. Inverting it will cause all subsequent binary bits to be wrong, leading to incorrect Gray code output.
candidates.spec_basis: The implementation should follow this process: 1. Input a Gray code value, 2. Convert the Gray code to binary representation
